title.narrative: Infrastructure Improvement for Shrimp Aquaculture Project

description.narrative: The project will help the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries (MMAF) to introduce sustainable shrimp aquaculture to increase the productivity, quality, profitability, and environmental sustainability of shrimp farming by smallholders. The project will improve smallholder farmers' access to quality inputs, production, and post-harvest practices and traceability through infrastructure, capacity support, and value chain strengthening in selected locations (Across Bali, Banten, Central Java, East Java, Lampung, Nangro Aceh Darusalam, and South Sulawesi provinces). It is aligned with the following impact: contribution of the fisheries industries to the national economy increased. It will have the following outcome: productivity, profitability, and environment sustainability of shrimp aquaculture increased. Specifically, it will (i) increase quality and sustainability of inputs for shrimp production, (ii) develop sustainable and climate adaptive aquaculture infrastructure and services, and (iii) strengthen shrimp aquaculture supply chain.

Output: Quality and sustainability of inputs for shrimp production increased Indicator: A modern broodstock center with a capacity of 500,000 broodstock/year constructed, with disaster-resilient, gender-responsive, and gender-inclusive design features Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 1a-1b. Oceanic Institute (OI) of Hawaii Pacific University contracted on 1 November 2023 for Broodstock and Multiplication Centers Advisory Services with following progress: - Basic Criteria of BC delivered by OI to MMAF in end-March 2024 and MBC received 15 May 2024
- NES-1 trial, stocking shrimp seed received from Hawaii at BPIU2K on 15 June 2024. Broodstock from selected NES-1 families are in OI's NBC maturation system. In addition, “surplus” broodstock from selected NES-1 families are being held in a 75-m2 raceway in case they are needed for NES-3 production. NES-1 trial, completed and harvested on June 2024
- NES-2 trial, stocking shrimp seed received from Hawaii at BPIU2K on 12 December 2024 in Karangasem. NES-2 families are currently being evaluated for growout performance. Data from the NES-2 trials in Indonesia and at OI will be used to select families for the production of NES-4. NES-2 trial, completed and harvested on February 24, 2025
- For NES-3, about 400 shrimp from 18 selected NES-1 families are in OI's maturation system. They are being prepared (SPF, fresh feeds) to spawn in early February 2025.
- OI has created and submitted a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) with Progress Report No. 5 (Year Two), which serves as a living document.
- Inputs were provided for the DED to incorporate gender-responsive and inclusive design features, including accessible entrances, ramps, separate toilets for men and women, adequate spacing between brood tanks, and evacuation facilities.
- The procurement of construction of broodstock center and laboratories civil package, CW-01, was officially advertised on 19 December 2025 with the tender deadline set on 15 January 2026. This package is expected to be awarded in Q2 2026
Data Source: Project progress reports and surveys

Output: Sustainable and climate adaptive aquaculture infrastructure and services developed Indicator: At least 521 farmers' groups established and strengthened, of which at least 20% have women on their committees Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 2a-2b. The PMTC with the facilitators recruited by MMAF regional technical office (UPT/ Balai) will support establishment of farmers groups. A total of 300 farmer groups have been established and/or strengthened, with 69% having women represented in their committees, exceeding the 20% target
The draft SADPs have been prepared for all locations. Awaiting completion of economic and financial analyses. In principle, all locations have baseline data and initial drafts, but some drafts still requiring significant improvements. Lampung Selatan SADP shall serve as a reference for finalizing the other locations.
As agreed between MMAF and ADB, the SADP will be developed per district, not per farmers groups. The number of SADPs to be prepared and the total number of target farmer groups shall be adjusted in accordance to the agreement made with MMAF and Bappenas during the MTR mission fielded in September 2025.
Data Source: Project progress reports and surveys
